heading: One half is always sorted
body:
When you split a rotated sorted array, **at least one half is always sorted**. Compare `nums[left]` with `nums[mid]`: if `nums[left] <= nums[mid]`, the left half is sorted; otherwise the right half is.

Once you know which half is sorted, check if the target falls in that range—then discard the other half.

heading: The rotation trick
body:
**Gotcha:** Don't linear scan.

Even though the array is rotated, binary search still works—you just need to figure out which half to discard. Check the sorted half's endpoints to decide:
- `nums[left] <= target < nums[mid]` → search left
- `nums[mid] < target <= nums[right]` → search right

label: Crux · Python

q: What is the time complexity of this solution?
explain: Binary search halves the search space each iteration, even with rotation—O(log n).
